thread:
mira: ran an overnight regional sweep across A100 vs H100 for llama-2-7b and mosaic-7b. raw CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-infer-bench/1902468100-sweep.csv. quick take: H100 wins latency & steady-state tok/s on decode; A100 gets closer with larger batching but has worse p95 tail. nf4 helps both, more uplift on H100.

jon: can you drop the core numbers (tok/s, prefill p50/p95, $/1M) so i can share a one-pager?

mira: yep 5 pasted median of 3 runs per region. per-GPU numbers, batch=1 decode unless noted.

```
Model: llama-2-7b
Region: us-west1
 H100-80GB: prefill p50 78ms, p95 185ms | decode 2600 tok/s | $/1M tokens = $4.3
 A100-40GB: prefill p50 125ms, p95 360ms | decode 1400 tok/s | $/1M tokens = $7.9

Region: eu-west1
 H100: prefill p50 92ms, p95 220ms | decode 2350 tok/s | $/1M = $4.9
 A100: prefill p50 145ms, p95 410ms | decode 1200 tok/s | $/1M = $9.1

Region: asia-east1
 H100: prefill p50 115ms, p95 290ms | decode 1850 tok/s | $/1M = $5.8
 A100: prefill p50 170ms, p95 470ms | decode 900 tok/s  | $/1M = $10.8

Model: mosaic-7b
Region: us-west1
 H100: prefill p50 70ms, p95 170ms | decode 2800 tok/s | $/1M = $4.0
 A100: prefill p50 110ms, p95 330ms | decode 1500 tok/s | $/1M = $7.4
```

Quantized (nf4) notes (us-west1):
 H100 nf4: decode +60% -> ~4200 tok/s | cost ~ $2.6 /1M | small quality delta (~0.5% relative)
 A100 nf4: decode +45% -> ~2150 tok/s | cost ~ $4.3 /1M | similar small quality delta

kevin: what kernels/builds did you run? any flags that explain the H100 lead?

mira: kernel/config notes:
 - H100: cutlass + flash-attn2 + our fused KV-cache kernels, fp16 main path, nf4 via our compile-time quant patch. decode uses fused attention + optimized rematerialization for KV.
 - A100: cutlass-legacy + aten fallbacks for some attention shapes; decode fused path less efficient at batch=1 on A100.
 - batching: baseline runs are batch=1. A100 throughput approaches H100 at batch=8-16 for long-running throughput tests but p95 increases substantially (tail amplification).
 - CLI used for benching:
```
./bench --model <model> --gpu <H100|A100> --batch 1 --seq_prefill 512 --seq_decode 128 --quant <fp16|nf4>
```

sylvia: did you run any automated evals on nf4 for instruction prompts? hallucination or correctness regressions?

mira: quick eval on our 1200-instruction set: nf4 -> median accuracy drop ~0.8% for llama-2-7b, ~0.6% for mosaic-7b. some examples show higher variance but not catastrophic. planning longer run with adversarial subset before recommending nf4 for customer endpoints.

perf-bot: aggregate median cost (fp16 across models/regions): H100 ~ $4.9 /1M tokens, A100 ~ $8.9 /1M tokens. nf4 median: H100 ~ $3.0 /1M, A100 ~ $4.8 /1M.

jon: guidance for Dedicated sizing? e.g., GPUs needed for X tok/s steady state.

mira: rough rules-of-thumb:
 - H100-80GB: ~2.2k-2.8k tok/s per GPU on 7B (batch=1 decode). so for sustained 25k tok/s -> ~9-12 H100s.
 - A100-40GB: ~0.9k-1.6k tok/s per GPU on same workload. so 25k tok/s -> ~16-28 A100s depending on batch.
 - nf4 reduces counts by ~30-50% depending on kernel maturity and memory headroom.
 - caveat: prefill-heavy or long-context workloads reduce effective tok/s; size to worst-case p95 if SLA important.

kevin: should we surface a simple chart in console: tokens/sec vs cost for H100 vs A100 (fp16 & nf4)? i can mock a small viz.

mira: yes please 5 plot per-region curves and overlay p95 latency bands. note: callout that A100 improves with batching but tail latency rises; prefer batch=1 path for PLG traffic.

jon: created ticket INF-2350 attaching CSV + this thread. assigning kevin (viz) and sylvia (extended evals). thanks :thumbsup:

mira: thanks all 5 will run mixed-batch tests and longer nf4 eval overnight and post results.
